Fix stack overflow in git-find script

Fix stack overflow in git-find script (fixes #3)

This commit fixes two issues in the git-find script:

1. Stack overflow in assign_name method: Converted from recursive to
   iterative implementation using a queue-based approach. This prevents
   stack overflow when processing commits with very deep parent chains
   or complex histories. The iterative version can handle arbitrarily
   deep chains without hitting Ruby's stack limit.

2. ARGV handling bug: Fixed incorrect treatment of ARGV[0] as an array.
   Changed ARGV[0] to ARGV on lines 186 and 243 to properly handle
   command line arguments.

These changes resolve the SystemStackError reported when running git-find
on repositories with complex commit histories like the official Git repo.

Prevent .pyc bytecode cache from corrupting Nix store

On macOS the Nix store is not mounted read-only, so importing
dirscan.py would create __pycache__/ inside the store path,
silently corrupting its NAR hash and breaking substitution to
other machines. Set PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 via makeWrapperArgs.

Use buildPythonApplication so wrapPythonPrograms sets up PYTHONPATH

The previous approach used stdenv.mkDerivation with manual makeWrapper
calls, which only worked for direct `nix build` usage. When installed via
home-manager's buildPythonPackage, the scripts couldn't find the dirscan
module because dirscan.py wasn't in site-packages.

Switch to buildPythonApplication with format = "other" so that:
- dirscan.py is installed to $out/lib/python3.x/site-packages/
- wrapPythonPrograms (built into buildPythonApplication) automatically
  makes dirscan importable from all wrapped scripts
- All scripts (cleanup, verify, share, dirscan) are properly wrapped

Also add shebang to dirscan.py so wrapPythonPrograms can detect and
wrap it as a Python script.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.6 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Install all executable scripts with proper PYTHONPATH in Nix package

The Nix package previously only installed dirscan.py and created a single
dirscan wrapper. The helper scripts (cleanup, verify.py, share.py) were
not installed, and dirscan.py was not on PYTHONPATH, so `from dirscan
import *` would fail. Fix by placing dirscan.py in a proper module
